attrs.title: Suspensions we help with
attrs.lead: The reasons Google gives most often.

items.title: Misrepresentation
items.text: The most common suspension. Google thinks your ads or website could mislead people: missing contact details, unclear pricing, hidden fees, no returns policy, or claims you can’t back up. We check the site the way a Google reviewer would and fix what’s missing.

items.title: Circumventing systems
items.text: Google believes someone tried to get around its reviews: cloaking, links to an account suspended before, or ads changed to avoid policies. It’s serious and often permanent, so we look carefully at the account history before anything is sent.

items.title: Unacceptable business practices
items.text: Google suspects the business itself could harm people, for example by hiding who runs it or taking payment without delivering. We help you show who you are, with verification, real reviews and clear terms.

items.title: Suspicious payment activity
items.text: Declined cards, billing details that don’t match, or a payment method used on other accounts can trigger a suspension. We help verify billing and explain the payment history to Google.

items.title: Unpaid balance and billing issues
items.text: An unpaid invoice or failed payment can pause or suspend an account. Usually the quickest to fix, once the right payment profile and documents are in place.

items.title: Advertiser verification failed
items.text: If identity or business documents don’t match, or the deadline passes, ads stop. We check exactly which documents Google needs and help you resubmit them correctly.

attrs.noteText: A second rejected appeal makes the next one harder. We fix what Google is likely to check first, then appeal once, properly.

What happens after you contact us

Fast, careful and honest about the outcome. Here is what happens, day by day.

  1. We read the suspension email, your account history, linked accounts, billing and your website, the way a Google policy reviewer would.

    You get: A first call the same or next working day.

    • The suspension notice and the policy named
    • Account, billing and linked-account history
    • Your website checked page by page
    • Any previous appeals and Google’s replies

  2. We tell you the most likely cause in plain English, what needs to change, and honestly how strong your case is.

    You get: Written findings within 48 hours.

    • The most likely cause, and why we think so
    • A fix list in order of importance
    • Who makes each change: us or your team
    • An honest view of your chances

  3. Our developers update the website and we sort out the account issues: contact details, policies, claims, verification and billing.

    You get: Every change logged with before and after screenshots.

    • Contact, address and company details added
    • Returns, shipping and privacy policies published
    • Claims removed or backed up
    • Billing and verification checked

  4. We write one clear appeal that explains what was wrong and what changed, and send it with you from your account.

    You get: The appeal, sent once and properly.

    • Written in plain, factual language
    • Evidence of each change attached
    • Sent through the right Google form
    • A copy kept for your records

  5. We handle Google’s questions, and if the answer is no, we give you a clear plan for what to do next.

    You get: A plan either way.

    • Replies to any questions from Google
    • Ads checked before they go live again
    • A plan B if the appeal is refused
    • Tips to avoid future suspensions

attrs.title: Why accounts get suspended
attrs.lead: Google’s email names a policy, but rarely the exact problem. These are the issues we find behind most suspensions, and how we fix each one.

items.title: No contact details
items.problem: No address, phone number or company details on the website, so Google can’t tell who is behind the ads.
items.fix: Clear contact and business details on every page, matching your Google Ads account.

items.title: Missing policies
items.problem: Returns, refund or shipping policies are missing, vague or hard to find.
items.fix: Clear policies, written for your business and linked from the footer and checkout.

items.title: Claims you can’t prove
items.problem: Claims like “#1”, “guaranteed results” or “lowest price” with nothing to back them up.
items.fix: Claims removed, reworded or supported with evidence such as awards or reviews.

items.title: Linked accounts
items.problem: Several accounts share a payment card or users with one that was suspended before.
items.fix: Account links reviewed, removed where needed and explained in the appeal.

items.title: Payment problems
items.problem: A payment failed, or the billing details looked unusual to Google.
items.fix: Billing verified, the payment profile corrected and the payment history explained.

attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: Why was my Google Ads account suspended?
items.answer: Google suspends accounts for serious or repeated policy issues, such as misrepresentation, circumventing systems, unacceptable business practices or suspicious payments. The email names the policy, but rarely the exact problem.

items.question: What does misrepresentation mean in Google Ads?
items.answer: Google believes your ads or website could mislead people, for example by hiding who you are, how to contact you, what things cost or what your policies are.

items.question: How long does a Google Ads appeal take?
items.answer: Usually a few days to a few weeks. Sending an appeal without fixing the cause often leads to a quick rejection.

items.question: Can you guarantee my account will be reinstated?
items.answer: No. Only Google can reinstate an account. We fix the likely causes and prepare a strong appeal, and we’re honest about the chances.

items.question: Should I open a new account?
items.answer: No. Creating new accounts to get around a suspension breaks Google’s policies and usually leads to more suspensions.
